newsitem.title: USA: LATE NYMEX NATGAS STILL DOWN, LONGS TAKE PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: LATE NYMEX NATGAS STILL DOWN, LONGS TAKE PROFITS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained lower late Wednesday in slower trade, still pressured by light profit taking after recent gains despite reports of firmer physical prices, market sources said.
At 1410 EDT, September slipped 2.8 cents to $2.346 per million British thermal units. October was 3.1 cents lower at $2.35. Most others were down by one-half to four cents.

"Basically, this is a technically-driven market without a lot of fundamental backing, but you don't want to get in the way of it with funds buying," said one Texas-based trader, noting light profit taking pressured the complex today.

While record heat out West and decent injection demand could underpin physical prices near-term, many remain skeptical current levels can be sustained without a broader heat wave to stir better cooling demand.
Extended forecasts are calling for mostly normal to below-normal temperatures for the eastern half of the nation, with the Southwest expected to remain hot.
And chart traders, while conceding a bullish technical picture after Friday's breakout, were still expecting a pullback after an 11 percent rally in five sessions.
They noted the sharp growth in open interest this week, up more than 15,000 lots in three days, indicating plenty of new length in the market.

Minor support in September was pegged at $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.20, then at $2.15-2.16 and along the short-term up trendline at $2.13. Resistance was seen at the new contract high of $2.43, whick also coincides with the May 7 spot continuation high, and then in the $2.48 area.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected a 70-75 bcf weekly stock build when the AGA report is released later today. For the same week last year, stocks gained 84 bcf.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed almost five cents to the mid-$2.30s. Midcon pipes were up a few cents to near the $2.30 level. New York city gate prices held relatively steady in the low-$2.50s.
NYMEX said 27,794 contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On the KCBT, September firmed one cent to $2.26, while deferreds were steady to four cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.8 cents to 8.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
